glossary.definition: a judgment that its member, an export's patient, is the subject, so every record naming that patient is the subject's.
what a reply says the records lack: the codes and words a record of it would carry (`match`), what was looked through (`coverage`), and the tool call (`query`) or the files (`sources`) that looked.
one thing done to a pod that writes files to it: an import, an entry session, a connection to a hospital's server, or a run of the matcher.
on a call's result, the name of the act the call made.
the program that converts an export into records; `import` loads it on first use.
a pod's identifier, made once when the pod is made: `pod://`, a random UUID and a slash.
the rows a question returns from a pod.
of an absence, borne out by what was looked through; an absence that is not comes back with `backed: false` and a `reason`.
Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's standard for the XML summary documents patient portals hand out.
one tab-separated value on a line of a compact read, under the column name the view's first line gives.
where a fact points (`cite`): a view entry, a FHIR resource in a download, or a line of one. In a reply about downloads it also gives, field by field, what the fact says the record there holds.
to say that an export's patient is the owner: the owner claims a profile by filing an About judgment. A patient no one has claimed is unclaimed, and its records are stored but shown in no answer.
the public archive, kept by the US National Library of Medicine, of how laboratories classify variants, from benign to pathogenic; one of the reference tables.
a published list of codes for one kind of thing, such as RxNorm for medicines, LOINC for lab tests and SNOMED CT for clinical findings.
a variant written in HGVS notation against a gene's transcript, such as `NM_000249.3:c.2042C>T`.
the whole pod as tab-separated text, which the `ask` tool returns a part at a time when called with `format: "compact"`; each line is one row of a view, its cells separated by tabs.
the organisation that keeps a document and answers for its true copy.
a judgment that its members are separate things; it overrules a Same of the two.
a file of a person's records as a hospital's server or portal gave it, before any import: FHIR resources in JSON, or a C-CDA document.
one call of `pod.enter()`: the act that files what the owner typed, as one owner-entered record or several, under a `urn:uuid:` name the app makes once.
a judgment that its members are wrong; they are left out of every answer.
what a person downloads of their own records: an Apple Health export, or a C-CDA document from a patient portal.
one record an item rests on: what the model says of it, and where it is.
a published list of the versions of reference tables, which an app reads to find newer ones.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: HL7's standard for health records as JSON.
one kind of thing a record says: its `value`, `unit`, `status`, `code`, `name` or `id`, a date (`date`, `start`, `end`, `recorded`), or its text (`text`, from which a `quote` is taken).
something the matcher noticed about a pod's records and filed for the owner to answer with a judgment.

a compact read's short name for a view entry: a letter for its view, then the first eight or more hexadecimal digits of the view entry's name, such as `L41e35923`. `ask` takes a list of them in `entries` to return only those view entries' rows.
the snapshot of this app's latest act in a pod.
the one file of a sealed pod left readable, `settings/encryption.json`, which says how the pod is sealed.
the app's code that runs the tools for a model and gives them the functions they reach pods through (`PodReads`); in Node, `podReads()` makes one.
a laboratory's flag on a result, such as `H` for high.
one point of a reply, with what it rests on.
of a record, to be put with the records of a view entry by a judgment, a Same or the matcher's; the view entry is then named for its least record, so its name, and the handle made from it, changes.
a conclusion about records, made by a person or by a machine.
an answer to a named question saved beside the pod's folder, and returned again while nothing it was worked out from has changed.
a story and the exports it uses, which the vocabulary carries for testing, such as `alex-rivera`.
a choice of which judgments count when a question is answered: `everyday` is the default, and `export` is stricter, for records sent elsewhere.
what the reference tables say about one code, such as its name.
on a call's result, the result of the matcher's run that followed it.
the part of a runtime that compares a pod's records and writes a Same for those its rules find to be one thing, such as one allergy reported by two sources.
a record a judgment is about.
a language model that an app lets answer a person's questions about their records.
`document.modelContext`, the browser API proposed as WebMCP through which a web page offers tools to a model the browser runs.
a query the vocabulary carries under a name, such as `pod/My active allergies`.
the part of a C-CDA document written for a person to read, as table rows, list items and paragraphs, beside its coded records; a narrative line or row is one of those.
the dotted number by which a C-CDA document names a code system, such as `2.16.840.1.113883.6.1` for LOINC.
the person who keeps a pod and decides what its records mean; in every pod on this page, the subject acting for themselves.
a record the owner typed in themselves and filed with `pod.enter()`, such as an allergy they know they have; no source holds it, and being the owner's own it needs no claim.
one file holding all of a sample's files, so a page fetches them at once.
a set of lab tests reported together, such as a thyroid panel.
the snapshot that an act's snapshot names as the one before it; a pod's first snapshot has none.
a date that gives only a year, or a year and a month.
the person an export's records are about, as that source knows them, before anyone has said who they are in the pod.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
one source's record of its patient, which the owner claims; `claimedProfiles` and `unclaimedProfiles` list them.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
when a record was written down, as against when the thing it records happened: a C-CDA record's author time, a report's issue time.
the span of values a laboratory calls normal for a test, printed beside a result.
public code lists, such as RxNorm for medicines, that tell a runtime when two codes mean one thing.
the error thrown when the package declines a request it understood, such as a name it does not have; it has written nothing.
on a call's result, why a rule turned the call down; a refused call wrote nothing.
a model's answer to a person's question about their records, as JSON.
the form a reply must take: an `answer`, a `short` form of it, and `items`. `replySchema` is its JSON Schema, and `replyErrors()` lists where a reply departs from it.
one record in FHIR, named by its type and its id, such as `Observation/ldl-1`.
a numbered requirement in the vocabulary that every runtime must meet, such as A14 in `runtime/arrivals.feature`; a heading on this page links the rules its API reaches.
software that reads and writes pods as the vocabulary requires; this package is one.
a judgment that its members are one thing, so answers show them once.
a kit's pod saved as files a web page can read.
of a pod or a file, encrypted on disk so that only the secret opens it.
the six words that open an encrypted pod; `sixWords()` draws them from the EFF long word list, a public list of 7,776 easy-to-type words.
one of the reference tables across its versions, such as RxNorm's product ingredients.
the set of files a pod held as one act left it, which names the snapshot before it as a git commit names its parent.
one hospital server, or one document, whose records an export holds.
a compact read's name for a source: `S1`, `S2` and so on, each listed with who wrote it.
the W3C query language for data written as statements, as Turtle writes them; `pod.ask()` runs an app's own SPARQL SELECT.
one scripted action on a pod, such as making it, an import, an entry session or a judgment, named by a letter and a number such as `J10`.
the steps taken with one made-up patient's exports, in order.
a model provider's feature that makes a model reply in a given JSON Schema; providers take only some of JSON Schema's keywords.
the person a pod is about.
one word the vocabulary defines, named by an IRI, a web-style identifier such as `https://ns.cascadeprotocol.org/cascade#allergen`.
codes, words, a day and a kind of record that the caller holds an absence to as well as the absence's own, passed as `tied`; the evals take them from their answer key.
a function a model may call: a name, a description, a JSON Schema for its input, and the code that runs it.
one run of a tool by a model: the tool's name, the input it was given, whether it succeeded, and what it returned.
a W3C text format for writing statements in the vocabulary's terms; `pod.enter()` and `pod.judge()` take it.
the `Refusal` thrown when a pod does not open with the secret given, or with none; its `outcome` gives the reason, such as `incorrect secret`.
a difference in one of a person's genes from the reference sequence, as a genetic test reports it.
what a record says at one time; when a source changes a record, the pod keeps the old version and adds a new one. (Of a reference table or the runtime, "version" has its everyday meaning.)

a pod's records of one kind, such as medications, as its judgments leave them: one line for each thing however many sources reported it. A named question such as `pod/My medication history` returns a view's rows.
one thing in a view, such as one medication or one lab result: the records that are one thing, shown as one. A row names it in `entry`, by an IRI that ends in `#` and 64 hexadecimal digits.
cascade-vocabulary, the project that defines the words health data is written in, the requirements every pod meets, and a set of ready-made questions.
of a record, said by its own source not to be so: refuted, ruled out, entered in error, negated or nullified.
